intent: session cleanup Phase 3 Commit E: retire vendor-transcript archaeology
notes: Phase 3 Commit E of the [2026-08-11 non-Enterprise session cleanup plan](vault/artifacts/2026-08-11-non-enterprise-session-cleanup-plan.md) — the point-of-no-return deletion pass. Retires vendor-transcript archaeology from base Gator now that the Enterprise transcripts-first substrate (v2.6.0) is the source of truth for full transcript custody. Commit D unblocked this by removing all `gator-audit.py` references first.

Deleted 4 source files (~2,244 lines total): `src/gator_command/scripts/gator-sessions.py` (1,244 lines — vendor-agnostic orchestration CLI + spool/manifest/export/pending/commit-summaries subcommands; the 2 KEEP fns `parse_committed_summary` + `read_committed_summaries` were extracted to `gator_session_reader.py` in Phase 2A), `gator-session-sink.py` (831 lines — SQLite/DuckDB/NDJSON sink over spool + committed summaries), `gator-session-block.py` (680 lines — session-block companion capture; inert since v2.6.0 P1.3 stripped the post-commit-hook invocation), `extract-claude-sessions.py` (489 lines — Claude Code JSONL archaeology; superseded by Enterprise-cli's `transcripts_discovery.py`).

Deleted 3 test files (~97 tests total): `tests/test_sessions.py` (45 tests — `TestReadCommittedSummaries` migrated to `tests/test_session_reader.py` in Phase 2A; the other 12 classes exercised DELETE-VENDOR paths), `tests/test_session_sink.py`, `tests/test_session_block.py`.

`pyproject.toml`: removed `"scripts/gator-session-block.py"` from `[tool.setuptools.package-data]` (the only retired file that had been listed; the others were never in package-data — a pre-existing base-wheel gap flagged in the cross-cutting charter as follow-on).

Deferred to Phase 4 per parent plan §5 decision 2(b): `extract-codex-sessions.py` (477 lines) + `extract-gemini-sessions.py` (410 lines) — retire once Enterprise-side Codex + Gemini adapters ship. Shipping the vendor-coverage regression against Codex/Gemini users now would be a real product downgrade against the "multi-vendor governance" positioning.

Charter updates: **INDEX.md** — session-archaeology row rewritten to reflect surviving files only (`extract-codex-sessions`, `extract-gemini-sessions`, `gator-session-aggregator`, `gator-session-common`, `gator_session_reader`). **scripts-session-archaeology.md** — `**Covers**` line + Owns bullets + Does-Not-Own bullets rewritten; a `PHASE 3 STATUS` banner at the top marks that Commit F (session-common fold + full retitle) is still pending. The deep function-entry sections (extract-claude, gator-sessions, gator-session-sink, gator-session-block prose) intentionally left in place for Commit F's wholesale rewrite — they surface as "stale-charter-refs" warnings, non-blocking. **scripts-cross-cutting.md** — `parse_committed_summary` TRIPWIRE section collapsed to reflect the single-owner post-Phase-3 shape (one owner + two consumers, was 1 owner + 4 consumers); the graceful-degradation note now explicitly flags the base-wheel package-data gap as pre-existing.

Verification: full test suite **770 passed, 2 xfailed** (both pre-existing v2.6.0 xfails on v1 `active-vendor-session.json` compat — unrelated). The 97-test drop matches the 3 deleted test files exactly (45 + 27 + 25 ≈ 97). Zero regressions in surviving tests. `tests/test_audit_integration.py` (3 tests) still exercises `assemble_audit_data` end-to-end through the snippet-reader path — passes clean.

Significance-check assessment (constitution step 7): SIGNIFICANT — touches cross-module invariants (retires 4 files that had documented cross-file consumers), retires the `parse_committed_summary` legacy copy (was one of 4 consumers in the r0 TRIPWIRE state; TRIPWIRE section updated). No public CLI verb affected (`sessions` was never a public `gator` verb; retired subcommands `sessions {index, manifest, export, pending, commit-summaries, turn-manifest, grep-turns, show-turns}` were internal-only entry points reachable only via direct script invocation). No security-relevant code. Steelman argument against: this collapses base Gator's ability to discover raw vendor transcripts entirely — anyone whose evidence workflow depended on `gator sessions <subcommand>` invocation must move to Enterprise or rely on snippet-based governance. Response: this is exactly the ratified direction — parent plan §3 states "Base Gator removes raw-vendor-transcript discovery, per-vendor extractors, transcript sink, session-block generator, and all their tests + CLI subcommands. Enterprise remains the source of truth for full transcript custody + audit linkage (unchanged by this cleanup)." No new-user surface loss (transcripts-first has been the ratified direction since v2.6.0, 2026-08-11); existing users who were on the vendor-discovery path have Enterprise-cli's `transcripts_discovery.py` for Claude (Codex/Gemini deferred to Phase 4 per §5 decision 2(b)).
